Thus corruptly M, where the scholiast, who noted εἷς ὑπὲρ τῶν Αίγυπτίων πρεσβεύοι [one should act as envoy on behalf of the Egyptians], seems to have read λύμας, εἷς δὲ πρὸ γᾶς ὑλάσκοι, λύμας εἷς σύ πρὸ γᾶς ὑλάσκων [ruins, one should bark before the land, ruins, you alone before the land barking] Weilius. The usual form of the verb is ὑλάω [to bark], ὑλάσκω [to bark] is nowhere else read, so it is not improbable that it is corrupted from λάσκει [he cries out], which is Paleius' conjecture, who wrote οἰοῖ οἰοῖ λύμας · ἄγρια γὰρ σὺ λάσκεις [alas, alas, ruins; for you cry out wild things].
